52:1: Interpretation of Surat At-Tur Malik narrated from al-Zuhri from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im from his father: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite Surat al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, and I never heard anyone with a better voice or recitation than him. They both narrated it on the authority of Malik. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Malik narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal from Urwah from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah from Umm Salamah who said: I complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that I was ill, so he said: Tawaf behind the people while you are riding. So I performed the tawaf and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying beside the House, reciting Surat al-Tur and the Inscribed Book. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God swears by His creations, which indicate His great power, that His punishment will befall His enemies, and that He has no protector from them. The Mount is the mountain on which there are trees, like the one on which God spoke to Moses and from which He sent Jesus. Whatever does not have trees is not called a Mount, but rather it is called a mountain. And an Inscribed Book. It was said: It is the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: The revealed written books that are read to the people aloud. That is why He said: “On parchment spread out. And the Frequented House.” It was proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith of the Night Journey after passing through the seventh heaven: Then I was taken up to the Frequented House, and behold, seventy thousand enter it every day and do not return to it, the last thing they are required to do. That is, they worship in it and circumambulate it as the people of the earth circumambulate their Kaaba. Likewise, that Frequented House is the Kaaba of the people of the seventh heaven. That is why Abraham, peace and blessings be upon him, was found leaning his back against the Frequented House, because he is the builder of the earthly Kaaba, and the reward is of the same kind as the work, and it is opposite the Kaaba. In every heaven there is a house in which its people worship and pray to it, and that which is in The lowest heaven is called the House of Glory, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Ruh bin Janah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “In the seventh heaven there is a house called Al-Ma’mur opposite the Kaaba, and in the fourth heaven there is a river called Al-Hayawan, which Gabriel enters every day and immerses himself in it, then he comes out and shakes himself, and seventy thousand drops fall from it. God creates from every drop an angel who is commanded to come to Al-Bayt Al-Ma’mur and pray in it, and they do so, then they come out and never return to it again, and one of them is appointed over them and is commanded to stand with them in the heaven at a place where they glorify God until the Hour comes.” This is a very strange hadith, narrated only by Ruh bin Janah, who is the Qurashi Umayyad, their client, Abu Sa’d Al-Dimashqi. A group of hadith masters rejected this hadith, including Al-Jawzajani, Al-Uqaili, Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah Al-Naysaburi, and others. Al-Hakim said: It has no basis in the hadith of Abu Hurairah, Sa’id, or Al-Zuhri. Ibn Jarir said: Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, Abu Al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Samak bin Harb, from Khalid bin Arara, that a man said to Ali: What is Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur? He said: It is a house in the heaven called Ad-Dhirah, which is opposite the Kaaba, above it. Its sanctity in the heaven is like the sanctity of the House on earth. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, then they never return to it. This is how Shu'bah and Sufyan Al-Thawri narrated it from Samak, and according to them, Ibn Al-Kawwa' was the one asking about it. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Talq bin Ghannam, from Za'idah, from Asim, from Ali bin Rabi'ah, who said: Ibn Al-Kawwa' asked Ali about Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur. He said: It is a mosque in the heaven called Ad-Dhirah, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, then they never return to it. And he narrated it from the hadith of Abu Al-Tufayl, from Ali, in a similar manner. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas: It is a house opposite the Throne, which is frequented by angels. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, then they never return to it. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, and many others among the Salaf said. Qatada, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and As-Suddi said: It was reported to us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said one day to his companions: Do you know what Al-Bayt Al-Ma’mur is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “It is a mosque in the heaven opposite the Kaaba. If it were to collapse, it would collapse on it. Every day, seventy thousand angels pray in it. If they leave it, they will never return to it.” Ad-Dahhak claimed that it is inhabited by a group of angels called the jinn from the tribe of Iblis. God knows best. And God says: And the raised ceiling. Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Shu’bah, and Abu Al-Ahwas said, from Simak, from Khalid ibn Arara, from Ali. And the raised ceiling means the sky. Sufyan said: Then he recited: And We have made the heaven a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, turn away. Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ibn Jarir preferred this view. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: It is the Throne, meaning that it is a ceiling for all creation, and it has a direction, and it is intended along with others, as the majority said. God the Almighty says: {And the sea that is set ablaze.} Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It is the water beneath the Throne from which God sends down rain, by which the bodies in their graves will be revived on the Day of Resurrection. The majority said: It is this sea. There is disagreement over the meaning of His statement, set ablaze. Some of them said: What is meant is that a fire will be lit on the Day of Resurrection, like His statement, And when the seas are set ablaze. That is, they are set ablaze and become a blazing fire that surrounds the people of the gathering. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated it on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and this is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair and others said. Al-Ala' ibn Badr said: It was called the sea that is set ablaze because no water is drunk from it and no crops are irrigated by it. And so will the seas on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on his authority. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: And the sea that is set ablaze means sent. Qatadah said: Set ablaze is filled. Ibn Jarir chose this and explained it by saying that it is not set ablaze today, so it is full. It was also said that what is meant by it is empty. Al-Asma'i said, on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', on the authority of Dhi al-Rummah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: And the sealed sea, he said: Empty. A nation went out to pray for rain and returned saying: The pool is sealed, meaning empty. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in Masaneed al-Shu'ara'. It was said that what is meant by sealed is the one that is prevented and held back from the land so that it does not overflow and drown its people. This was said by Ali ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi and others say the same. This is indicated by the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, in his Musnad, for he said: Yazid told us, al-Awam told us, an old man who was stationed on the coast told me: I met Abu Salih, the freed slave of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is not a night but that the sea rises up three times, seeking God's permission to pour water over them, and God, the Almighty and Majestic, restrains it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili said: Al-Hasan bin Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Rahawayh, on the authority of Yazid, who is the son of Harun, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, who said: An old man from Marabit told me: I went out one night to my guard, and no one from the guard went out except me. I came to the port and climbed up, and it seemed to me that the sea was rising up, level with the tops of the mountains. It did that repeatedly while I was awake, so I met Abu Salih, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is not a night except that the sea rises up three times, asking God’s permission to pour out upon them, and God, the Almighty and Majestic, restrains it. There is an unknown man in it whose name was not mentioned. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. This is what the oath is sworn to be, meaning that it will come to pass upon the disbelievers, as He said in the other verse: There is none to avert it, meaning there is no one to avert it from them if God wills that upon them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya said: My father told us, Musa bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Salih Al-Mari, on the authority of Jaafar bin Zaid Al-Abdi, who said: “Umar went out on patrol in Madinah one night and passed by the house of a Muslim man. He happened to be praying, so he stopped to listen to his recitation and recited: ‘By the Mount * And a Book Inscribed * On parchment spread out * And by the Much-Frequented House * And the raised ceiling * And the filled sea * Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass * There is none to avert it.’” He said: An oath, by the Lord of the Kaaba, is true. So he got off his donkey and leaned against a wall and stayed for a while, then he returned to his home. He stayed there for a month, and people visited him, not knowing what had ailed him, may God be pleased with him. Imam Abu Ubaid said in The Virtues of the Qur’an: Muhammad bin Salih told us, Hisham bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan that Umar recited: ‘Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass * There is none to avert it.’ So he recited it twenty days long. And the statement of God, the Most High: ‘The Day the heaven will shake with a shaking.’ Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It will shake with a shaking. And from Ibn Abbas: It means its cracking.” Mujahid said: It revolves. Ad-Dahhak said: Its rotation and movement are by the command of God and the waves of some of it in others. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, that it is the movement in a rotation. He said: Abu Ubaidah Muammar ibn al-Muthanna recited the verse of Al-A’sha and said: As if her walk from her neighbor's house was like a cloud, neither slowing down nor hurrying up. And the mountains will move meaning they will go and become scattered dust and be blown away. So woe on that Day to the deniers meaning woe to them on that Day from the torment and punishment of God upon them and His chastisement of them. Those who are in vain play meaning they are in this world vain in falsehood and take their religion as a mockery and a game. The Day they will be called meaning they will be pushed and driven to the fire of Hell, called Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi and Al-Thawri said: they will be pushed into it forcefully. This is the Fire which you used to deny meaning the guards will say that to them as a rebuke and a rebuke. Is this magic, or do you not see? * Enter it meaning enter it as one who is engulfed from all sides. So be patient or do not be patient; it is all the same to you meaning whether you are patient with its torment and punishment or not. There is no escape for you from it and no escape from it. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do meaning God will not wrong anyone, but will recompense everyone. By his work

That is why Abraham, peace and blessings be upon him, was found leaning his back against the Frequented House, because he is the builder of the earthly Kaaba, and the reward is of the same kind as the work, and it is opposite the Kaaba, and in every The sky is a house in which its inhabitants worship and pray to it, and the one in the lowest heaven is called the House of Glory, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Ruh bin Janah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “In the seventh heaven there is a house called Al-Ma’mur opposite the Kaaba, and in the fourth heaven there is a river called Al-Hayawan, which Gabriel enters every day and immerses himself in it, then he comes out and shakes himself, and seventy thousand drops fall from it. God creates from every drop an angel who is commanded to come to Al-Bayt Al-Ma’mur and pray in it, and they do so, then they come out and never return to it again, and one of them is appointed over them and is commanded to stand with them in the heaven at a place where they glorify God until the Hour comes.” This is a very strange hadith, narrated only by Ruh bin Janah, who is the Qurashi Umayyad, their client, Abu Sa’d Al-Dimashqi. A group of hadith masters rejected this hadith, including Al-Jawzajani, Al-Uqaili, Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah Al-Naysaburi, and others. Al-Hakim said: It has no basis in the hadith of Abu Hurairah, Sa’id, or Al-Zuhri. Ibn Jarir said: Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, Abu Al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Samak bin Harb, from Khalid bin Arara, that a man said to Ali: What is Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur? He said: It is a house in the heaven called Ad-Dhirah, which is opposite the Kaaba, above it. Its sanctity in the heaven is like the sanctity of the House on earth. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, then they never return to it. This is how Shu'bah and Sufyan Al-Thawri narrated it from Samak, and according to them, Ibn Al-Kawwa' was the one asking about it. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Talq bin Ghannam, from Za'idah, from Asim, from Ali bin Rabi'ah, who said: Ibn Al-Kawwa' asked Ali about Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur. He said: It is a mosque in the heaven called Ad-Dhirah, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, then they never return to it. And he narrated it from the hadith of Abu Al-Tufayl, from Ali, in a similar manner. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas: It is a house opposite the Throne, which is frequented by angels. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, then they never return to it. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, and many others among the Salaf said. Qatada, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and As-Suddi said: It was reported to us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said one day to his companions: Do you know what Al-Bayt Al-Ma’mur is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “It is a mosque in the heaven opposite the Kaaba. If it were to collapse, it would collapse on it. Every day, seventy thousand angels pray in it. If they leave it, they will never return to it.” Ad-Dahhak claimed that it is inhabited by a group of angels called the jinn from the tribe of Iblis. God knows best. And God says: And the raised ceiling. Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Shu’bah, and Abu Al-Ahwas said, from Simak, from Khalid ibn Arara, from Ali. And the raised ceiling means the sky. Sufyan said: Then he recited: And We have made the heaven a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, turn away. Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ibn Jarir preferred this view. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: It is the Throne, meaning that it is a ceiling for all creation, and it has a direction, and it is intended along with others, as the majority said. God the Almighty says: {And the sea that is set ablaze.} Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It is the water beneath the Throne from which God sends down rain, by which the bodies in their graves will be revived on the Day of Resurrection. The majority said: It is this sea. There is disagreement over the meaning of His statement, set ablaze. Some of them said: What is meant is that a fire will be lit on the Day of Resurrection, like His statement, And when the seas are set ablaze. That is, they are set ablaze and become a blazing fire that surrounds the people of the gathering. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated it on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and this is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair and others said. Al-Ala' ibn Badr said: It was called the sea that is set ablaze because no water is drunk from it and no crops are irrigated by it. And so will the seas on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on his authority. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: And the sea that is set ablaze means sent. Qatadah said: Set ablaze is filled. Ibn Jarir chose this and explained it by saying that it is not set ablaze today, so it is full. It was also said that what is meant by it is empty. Al-Asma'i said, on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', on the authority of Dhi al-Rummah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: "And the sealed sea," he said: Empty. A nation went out to pray for rain and returned saying: The pool is sealed, meaning empty. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in Masaneed al-Shu'ara'. It was said that what is meant by sealed is the one that is prevented and held back from the land so that it does not overflow and drown its people. This was said by Ali ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi and others say the same. This is indicated by the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, in his Musnad, for he said: Yazid told us, al-Awam told us, an old man who was stationed on the coast told me: I met Abu Salih, the freed slave of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "There is not a night but that the sea rises up three times, seeking God's permission to pour water over them, and God, the Almighty and Majestic, restrains it." Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili said: Al-Hasan bin Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Rahawayh, on the authority of Yazid, who is the son of Harun, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, who said: An old man from Marabit told me: I went out one night to my guard, and no one from the guard went out except me. I came to the port and climbed up, and it seemed to me that the sea was rising up, level with the tops of the mountains. It did that repeatedly while I was awake, so I met Abu Salih, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is not a night except that the sea rises up three times, asking God’s permission to pour out upon them, and God, the Almighty and Majestic, restrains it. There is an unknown man in it whose name was not mentioned. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. This is what the oath is sworn to be, meaning that it will come to pass upon the disbelievers, as He said in the other verse: There is none to avert it, meaning there is no one to avert it from them if God wills that upon them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya said: My father told us, Musa bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Salih Al-Mari, on the authority of Jaafar bin Zaid Al-Abdi, who said: “Umar went out on patrol in Madinah one night and passed by the house of a Muslim man. He happened to be praying, so he stopped to listen to his recitation and recited: ‘By the Mount * And a Book Inscribed * On parchment spread out * And by the Much-Frequented House * And the raised ceiling * And the filled sea * Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass * There is none to avert it.’” He said: An oath, by the Lord of the Kaaba, is true. So he got off his donkey and leaned against a wall and stayed for a while, then he returned to his home. He stayed there for a month, and people visited him, not knowing what had ailed him, may God be pleased with him. Imam Abu Ubaid said in The Virtues of the Qur’an: Muhammad bin Salih told us, Hisham bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan that Umar recited: ‘Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass * There is none to avert it.’ So he recited it twenty days long. And the statement of God, the Most High: ‘The Day the heaven will shake with a shaking.’ Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It will shake with a shaking. And from Ibn Abbas: It means its cracking.” Mujahid said: It revolves. Ad-Dahhak said: Its rotation and movement are by the command of God and the waves of some of it in others. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, that it is the movement in a rotation. He said: Abu Ubaidah Muammar ibn al-Muthanna recited the verse of Al-A’sha and said: As if her walk from her neighbor's house was like a cloud, neither slowing down nor hurrying up. And the mountains will move meaning they will go and become scattered dust and be blown away. So woe on that Day to the deniers meaning woe to them on that Day from the torment and punishment of God upon them and His chastisement of them. Those who are in vain play meaning they are in this world vain in falsehood and take their religion as a mockery and a game. The Day they will be called meaning they will be pushed and driven to the fire of Hell, called Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi and Al-Thawri said: they will be pushed into it forcefully. This is the Fire which you used to deny meaning the guards will say that to them as a rebuke and a rebuke. Is this magic, or do you not see? * Enter it meaning enter it as one who is engulfed from all sides. So be patient or do not be patient; it is all the same to you meaning whether you are patient with its torment and punishment or not. There is no escape for you from it and no escape from it. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do meaning God will not wrong anyone, but will recompense everyone. By his work
52:17: God the Almighty told us about the state of the happy ones, saying, Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure, which is the opposite of what those people are in of torment and punishment. Enjoying what their Lord has given them, meaning, they will enjoy what God has given them of pleasures of various kinds of pleasures, such as food, drink, clothing, homes, vehicles, and other things. And their Lord has saved them from the punishment of Hellfire, meaning, He has saved them from the punishment of the Fire. This is an independent blessing in and of itself, along with what is added to it of entering Paradise, which contains pleasures that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human mind has conceived. God the Almighty’s statement, Eat and drink at ease for what you used to do, is like His statement, Eat and drink at ease for what you put forth in the days past, meaning, this for that, out of His favor and kindness. And the Almighty said: Reclining on couches arranged in rows. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Hisayn on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Couches are in the chambers. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Sufyan bin Amr told us that he heard Al-Haytham bin Malik Al-Ta’i say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man may recline on a couch for the length of forty years, not moving from it or tiring of it, and whatever his soul desires and his eyes delight in will come to him. And my father told us, Hudbah bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin al-Mughira, on the authority of Thabit, who said: It has reached us that a man will recline in Paradise for seventy years with his wives and servants, and whatever God has given him of honor and bliss. Then when he looks around, he sees wives of his whom he had never seen before. They say, It is time for you to give us a share of you. The meaning of lined up is their faces facing each other, as in His saying, on thrones facing each other. “And We will marry them to houris of large, beautiful eyes,” meaning We will give them righteous companions and beautiful wives from among the houris. Mujahid said, And We will marry them means We will marry them to houris of large, beautiful eyes. Their description has been presented in more than one place, so there is no need to repeat it here.

52:21: God Almighty tells us about His grace, generosity, favor, and kindness in His creation and benevolence, that if the offspring of the believers follow them in faith, He will join them with their fathers in status, even if they do not reach their deeds, so that the fathers’ eyes may be comforted by the children with them in their homes. He will bring them together in the best way, by raising the one who has deficient deeds with perfect deeds, and that will not diminish his deeds and status, because of the equality between him and that one. For this reason, He said: We will join their offspring with them, and We have not deprived them of anything of their deeds. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Umar ibn Murrah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will raise the offspring of the believer in his degree, even if they are below him in deeds, so that His eyes may be comforted by them. Then he recited: And those who have believed and whose offspring follow them in faith, We will join them with their offspring, and We have not deprived them of anything of their deeds. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with it, and Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah with it, and al-Bazzar narrated it from Sahl ibn Bahr, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Hammad Al-Warraq, on the authority of Qais ibn Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He mentioned it and then said: Al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid ibn Yazid Al-Bayrouti told us, Muhammad ibn Shu’aib told me, Shaiban told me, Laith told me, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit Al-Asadi, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who have believed and whose offspring have followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, he said: They are the offspring of the believer who die in faith. If the status of their fathers was higher than their status, they will be joined with their fathers, and nothing will be deducted from the deeds that they did. Al-Hafiz Al-Tabarani said: Al-Husayn bin Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Muhammad bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghazwan told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, I think it was on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “When a man enters Paradise, he will be asked about his parents, his wife, and his children. It will be said that they did not reach your level. He will say: O Lord, you have worked for me and for them. Then he will be ordered to join them to him.” Ibn Abbas recited: And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith Al-Ma’idah 17:1-18. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: And those whose offspring attain faith and act in obedience to Me, I will join them with their faith in Paradise, and their young children will join them. This goes back to the first interpretation, for that is a clearer interpretation than this. This is what Al-Sha’bi, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Ibrahim, Qatadah, Abu Salih, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd say, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Uthman, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali, who said: Khadijah asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about two of her sons who died during the pre-Islamic period, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are in Hellfire. When he saw the hatred on her face, he said: If you saw where they were, you would hate them. She said: O Messenger of God, are my sons yours? He said: In Paradise. He said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Indeed, the believers and their children are in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children are in Hellfire. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: And those who have believed and whose offspring follow them in faith, the verse. This is God’s favor upon the children by the blessing of the fathers’ deeds. As for His favor upon the fathers by the blessing of the children’s supplications, Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Indeed, God raises the status of the righteous servant in Paradise, and he says: O Lord, how did I get this? He says: Because of your child’s supplication for you.” Its chain of transmission is sahih, and they did not narrate it from this source, but it has a corroborating evidence in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who supplicates for him.” And the Almighty’s saying: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned. When He informed about the station of grace, which is raising the status of offspring to the level of fathers without any action requiring that, He informed about the station of justice, which is that no one will be held accountable for the sin of another. So the Almighty said: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned. That is, pledged by his actions, and the sin of another person will not be held against him, whether he is a father or a son, as the Almighty said: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned, * Except the companions of the right hand, * In gardens, asking one another * About the criminals. And His saying: And We provided them with fruits and meat of whatever they desired. That is, We included them with fruits and meat of various kinds, of what is delicious and desired. His statement: They will dispute therein over a cup means they will drink therein a cup, that is, of wine. Ad-Dahhak said: There will be no idle talk therein nor will they commit sin meaning they will not speak therein vain talk, that is, delirium, nor sin, that is, obscene talk, as the drinkers of this world speak. Ibn Abbas said: Idle talk is falsehood, and sin is lying. Mujahid said: They will not insult each other nor will they commit sin. Qatada said: That was in this world with Satan, so God purified the wine of the Hereafter from the filth and harm of the wine of this world, as mentioned previously. He denied from it headaches, stomach pain, and the complete loss of reason. He informed that it does not lead them to bad, empty talk that contains delirium and obscenity. He informed of its beautiful appearance, pleasant taste, and its contents, saying: “White, a delight to those who drink. Therein is no evil, nor do they get headaches from it.” And He said: They will not get headaches from it, nor will they get headaches from it. And He said here: They will compete therein for a cup in which there is no vain talk or sin. And the Almighty’s statement: And there will circulate among them young boys as if they were hidden pearls is information about their servants and their retinue in Paradise, as if they were moist, hidden pearls in their beauty, splendor, cleanliness, and fine clothing, as the Almighty said: Immortal boys will circulate among them with goblets and pitchers and a cup from a pure spring. And the Almighty’s statement: And some of them will turn to others, asking one another. That is, they will turn to talk and ask one another. About their deeds and conditions in this world, and this is like the people of drinking talk about their drink when they are drunk, about what happened to them. They said, ‘Indeed, we were before among our families in fear’ meaning, we were in this world while we were among our families, fearing our Lord and fearing His punishment and chastisement. But God was gracious to us and saved us from the punishment of the scorching wind meaning, He was charitable to us and protected us from what we fear. Indeed, we used to call upon Him before meaning, we used to supplicate to Him, so He answered us and granted us our request. Indeed, He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. In this regard, a hadith was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar in his Musnad. He said: Salamah bin Shabib narrated to us, Saeed bin Dinar narrated to us, Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they will yearn for their brothers. One of them will come and touch the other’s bed, and they will talk. One of them will lean on his back and the other will lean on his back, and they will talk about what happened in the world. Then one of them will say to the other: ‘O so-and-so, do you know what day God forgave us? The day we were in such-and-such a place, and we supplicated to God, the Almighty, and He forgave us.’” Al-Bazzar then said: We do not know of it being narrated except through this chain of narration. I said: And Saeed bin Dinar Al-Dimashqi? Abu Hatim said: “He is unknown, and his sheikh is Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih. More than one has spoken about him with regard to his memory, but he is a righteous man, trustworthy in himself.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, that she recited this verse: “So God was gracious to us and saved us from the punishment of the scorching wind. Indeed, we used to supplicate to Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful.” So she said: O God, be gracious to us and save us from the punishment of the scorching wind. For this reason, He said: We will join their offspring with them, and We have not deprived them of anything of their deeds. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Umar ibn Murrah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will raise the offspring of the believer in his degree, even if they are below him in deeds, so that His eyes may be comforted by them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with it, and Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah with it, and al-Bazzar narrated it from Sahl ibn Bahr, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Hammad Al-Warraq, on the authority of Qais ibn Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said, ‘Indeed, we were before among our families in fear’ meaning, we were in this world while we were among our families, fearing our Lord and fearing His punishment and chastisement. But God was gracious to us and saved us from the punishment of the scorching wind meaning, He was charitable to us and protected us from what we fear. Indeed, we used to call upon Him before meaning, we used to supplicate to Him, so He answered us and granted us our request. Indeed, He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. In this regard, a hadith was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar in his Musnad. He said: Salamah bin Shabib narrated to us, Saeed bin Dinar narrated to us, Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they will yearn for their brothers. One of them will come and touch the other’s bed, and they will talk. One of them will lean on his back and the other will lean on his back, and they will talk about what happened in the world. Then one of them will say to the other: ‘O so-and-so, do you know what day God forgave us? The day we were in such-and-such a place, and we supplicated to God, the Almighty, and He forgave us.’” Al-Bazzar then said: We do not know of it being narrated except through this chain of narration. I said: And Saeed bin Dinar Al-Dimashqi? Abu Hatim said: “He is unknown, and his sheikh is Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih. More than one has spoken about him with regard to his memory, but he is a righteous man, trustworthy in himself.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, that she recited this verse: “So God was gracious to us and saved us from the punishment of the scorching wind. Indeed, we used to supplicate to Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful.” So she said: O God, be gracious to us and save us from the punishment of the scorching wind. Indeed, You are the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. Al-A’mash was asked: In prayer? He said: Yes.
52:28: God Almighty tells us about His grace, generosity, favor, and kindness in His creation and benevolence, that if the offspring of the believers follow them in faith, He will join them with their fathers in status, even if they do not reach their deeds, so that the fathers’ eyes may be comforted by the children with them in their homes. He will bring them together in the best way, by raising the one who has deficient deeds with perfect deeds, and that will not diminish his deeds and status, because of the equality between him and that one. For this reason, He said: We will join their offspring with them, and We have not deprived them of anything of their deeds. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Umar ibn Murrah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will raise the offspring of the believer in his degree, even if they are below him in deeds, so that His eyes may be comforted by them. Then he recited: And those who have believed and whose offspring follow them in faith, We will join them with their offspring, and We have not deprived them of anything of their deeds. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri with it, and Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah with it, and al-Bazzar narrated it from Sahl ibn Bahr, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Hammad Al-Warraq, on the authority of Qais ibn Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He mentioned it and then said: Al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid ibn Yazid Al-Bayrouti told us, Muhammad ibn Shu’aib told me, Shaiban told me, Laith told me, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit Al-Asadi, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who have believed and whose offspring have followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, he said: They are the offspring of the believer who die in faith. If the status of their fathers was higher than their status, they will be joined with their fathers, and nothing will be deducted from the deeds that they did. Al-Hafiz Al-Tabarani said: Al-Husayn bin Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Muhammad bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghazwan told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, I think it was on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “When a man enters Paradise, he will be asked about his parents, his wife, and his children. It will be said that they did not reach your level. He will say: O Lord, you have worked for me and for them. Then he will be ordered to join them to him.” Ibn Abbas recited: And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith Al-Ma’idah 17:1-18. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: And those whose offspring attain faith and act in obedience to Me, I will join them with their faith in Paradise, and their young children will join them. This goes back to the first interpretation, for that is a clearer interpretation than this. This is what Al-Sha’bi, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Ibrahim, Qatadah, Abu Salih, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd say, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Uthman, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali, who said: Khadijah asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about two of her sons who died during the pre-Islamic period, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are in Hellfire. When he saw the hatred on her face, he said: If you saw where they were, you would hate them. She said: O Messenger of God, are my sons yours? He said: In Paradise. He said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Indeed, the believers and their children are in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children are in Hellfire. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: And those who have believed and whose offspring follow them in faith, the verse. This is God’s favor upon the children by the blessing of the fathers’ deeds. As for His favor upon the fathers by the blessing of the children’s supplications, Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Indeed, God raises the status of the righteous servant in Paradise, and he says: O Lord, how did I get this? He says: Because of your child’s supplication for you.” Its chain of transmission is sahih, and they did not narrate it from this source, but it has a corroborating evidence in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who supplicates for him.” And the Almighty’s saying: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned. When He informed about the station of grace, which is raising the status of offspring to the level of fathers without any action requiring that, He informed about the station of justice, which is that no one will be held accountable for the sin of another. So the Almighty said: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned. That is, pledged by his actions, and the sin of another person will not be held against him, whether he is a father or a son, as the Almighty said: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned, * Except the companions of the right hand, * In gardens, asking one another * About the criminals. And His saying: And We provided them with fruits and meat of whatever they desired. That is, We included them with fruits and meat of various kinds, of what is delicious and desired. His statement: They will dispute therein over a cup means they will drink therein a cup, that is, of wine. Ad-Dahhak said: There will be no idle talk therein nor will they commit sin meaning they will not speak therein vain talk, that is, delirium, nor sin, that is, obscene talk, as the drinkers of this world speak. Ibn Abbas said: Idle talk is falsehood, and sin is lying. Mujahid said: They will not insult each other nor will they commit sin. Qatada said: That was in this world with Satan, so God purified the wine of the Hereafter from the filth and harm of the wine of this world, as mentioned previously. He denied from it headaches, stomach pain, and the complete loss of reason. He informed that it does not lead them to bad, empty talk that contains delirium and obscenity. He informed of its beautiful appearance, pleasant taste, and its contents, saying: “White, a delight to those who drink. Therein is no evil, nor do they get headaches from it.” And He said: They will not get headaches from it, nor will they get headaches from it. And He said here: They will compete therein for a cup in which there is no vain talk or sin. 52:29: God the Almighty commands His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to deliver His message to His servants and remind them of what God has revealed to him. Then He denies what the slanderers and immoral people accuse him of, saying: Then remind, for you are not, by the grace of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman. That is, I am not, praise be to God, a soothsayer as the ignorant infidels of Quraysh say. A soothsayer is one to whom a vision from the jinn comes with a word that he receives from heaven. Nor a madman, that is, one who is afflicted by Satan due to possession. Then God the Almighty says, denouncing their statement about the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: Or do they say, 'He is a poet for whom we are awaiting a misfortune of time?' That is, the calamities of time, and death is death. They say, We wait for him and are patient until death comes to him and we are relieved from him and his affair. God the Almighty says: Say, 'Wait, for I am with you among those who wait.' That is, wait, for I am waiting with you, and you will come to know for whom the outcome and victory will be in this world and the hereafter. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: When the Quraysh gathered in Dar al-Nadwa regarding the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one of them said: They have kept him in chains and are waiting for him to be destroyed by the vicissitudes of fate until he perishes as the poets who came before him perished, Zuhayr and al-Nabigha. He is like one of them. So God Almighty revealed this from their saying: Or do they say, ‘He is a poet; we are waiting for him to be destroyed by the vicissitudes of fate?’ Then God the Almighty said: {Or do their dreams command them to do this?} That is, do their minds command them to do this that they say about you of false statements that they know in themselves to be lies and fabrications. {Or are they a transgressing people?} That is, but they are a transgressing, misguided, obstinate people. This is what drives them to say what they said about you. And God the Almighty said: {Or do they say, You say it?} That is, he invented it and fabricated it on his own, meaning the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: {Rather, they do not believe.} That is, their disbelief is what drives them to this statement. {So let them produce a statement like it, if they should be truthful.} That is, if they are truthful in what they say about what they say and fabricate, then let them produce something like what Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought from this Qur’an. For if they and all the people of the earth, from the jinn and mankind, were to come together, they would not produce anything like it, nor ten surahs like it, nor a single surah like it.

52:35: This is the position in proving Lordship and Oneness of Divinity. God the Almighty said: "Or were they created by nothing? Or are they the creators?" Then God the Almighty said: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain. That is, did they create the heavens and the earth? This is a denial of their polytheism with God, even though they know that He is the Creator alone, with no partner, but their lack of certainty is what drives them to do that. Or do they have the treasures of your Lord, or are they the ones in control? That is, do they dispose of the kingdom and hold in their hands the keys to the treasuries? Or are they the ones in control? That is, are they the ones who hold creation to account? This is not the case. Rather, God the Almighty is the Owner, Disposer of affairs, and Doer of whatever He wills. And the Almighty said: Or do they have a ladder by which they listen? That is, a ladder to the highest assembly. Then let their listener bring clear proof. That is, let the one who listens to them bring clear evidence for the correctness of what they are doing and saying, that is, they have no way to do that, so they are not on anything and they have no proof. Then He said, denouncing them for what they attributed to Him of daughters and their making the angels females, and their choosing for themselves males over females, such that when one of them is given the good report of a female, his face remains dark and he is filled with inward grief. This is because they made the angels daughters of God and worshipped them along with God, so He said: Or does He have daughters and you have sons? This is a severe threat and a definite warning. Or do you ask them for a reward? Any reward for conveying God’s message to them, that is, you do not ask them for anything for that. So they are burdened with a heavy burden meaning, they are annoyed by the slightest thing, and it burdens them and makes it difficult for them. Or do they have the unseen, so they write meaning, the matter is not like that, for no one in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God. Or do they intend a plot? Then it is those who disbelieve who are the plotters. God the Almighty says: Or do these people intend, by what they say about the Messenger and the religion, to deceive the people and plot against the Messenger and his companions? Their plotting only brings its consequences upon themselves, so it is those who disbelieve who are the plotters. Or do they have a deity other than God? Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. This is a strong denunciation of the polytheists in their worship of idols and rivals with God. Then He exalted Himself above what they say, fabricate, and associate, saying: Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him.
52:44: God the Almighty says, informing about the polytheists' stubbornness and obstinacy regarding what is tangible: And if they see a fragment of the sky falling meaning that they are being punished by it, they would not believe it or be certain. Rather, they would say: This is just piled-up clouds, meaning that it has accumulated. This is like His Almighty’s saying: “And even if We opened to them a gate from the sky and they continued therein to ascend, * They would surely say, “Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people bewitched.” And God the Almighty said: So leave them meaning leave them, O Muhammad, until they meet their Day on which they will be struck dead and that is the Day of Resurrection The Day their plot will not avail them at all meaning their plotting and deceit that they used in this world will not benefit them at all on the Day of Resurrection nor will they be aided. Then God the Almighty said: And indeed, for those who do wrong is a punishment less than that meaning before that in this world, as He the Almighty said: And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment that perhaps they will return 1:11. For this reason God the Almighty said: But most of them do not know meaning We will punish them in this world and test them with calamities in it so that they may return and repent, but they do not understand what is intended for them. Rather, when what they were in is removed from them, they revert to the worst of what they were doing, as stated in some hadiths: When a hypocrite falls ill and recovers, he is like a camel in this respect; he does not know what they have understood or what they have been sent to do. And in the divine tradition: How much I disobey You and You do not punish me? God the Almighty said: O My servant, how much I will punish you and you do not know? And His statement: And be patient over the decision of your Lord, for indeed, you are before Our eyes means be patient with their harm and do not pay attention to them, for you are in Our sight and under Our protection, and God will protect you from the people. And His statement the Almighty: And exalt the praises of your Lord when you rise 1:11. Ad-Dahhak said: meaning to pray. Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, and blessed be Your name, and exalted be Your majesty, and there is no god but You. A similar hadith was narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Umar that he used to say: This at the beginning of the prayer. Ahmad and the Sunan scholars narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa’id and others, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he used to say that. Abu al-Jawza’ said: And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise meaning from your bed. Ibn Jarir preferred this view, and this statement is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated: Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Umair ibn Hani’ told us, Junada ibn Abi Umayya told me. Ubadah ibn as-Samit narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever wakes up at night and says: ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. Glory be to God and praise be to God. There is no god but God and God is Greatest. There is no power and no strength except with God.’ Then he says: ‘My Lord, forgive me’ - or he said: Then he supplicates - his prayer will be answered. If he resolves to do so, then performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted.” Al-Bukhari included it in his Sahih, and the scholars of Sunan included it on the authority of al-Walid ibn Muslim. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise, meaning: from every gathering. Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas: And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise, meaning: when a man wants to rise from his gathering, he should say: ‘Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You.’” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Nadr Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dimashqi told us, Muhammad ibn Shu`ayb told us, Talhah ibn `Amr al-Hadrami told me, on the authority of `Ata` ibn Abi Rabah, that he told him about the statement of God Almighty: And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise, meaning when you rise from every gathering, if you have done well, you will have increased in goodness, and if you were not, this will be an expiation for it. `Abd al-Razzaq said in his Jami`: Mu`mar told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, on the authority of Abu `Uthman al-Faqir, that Gabriel taught the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he rose from his gathering to say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You. Mu`mar said: And I heard others say that this statement is an expiation for gatherings. This is mursal, and it has been transmitted with a chain of transmission that strengthen each other with that. Among that is the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Whoever sits in a gathering and there is much idle talk, and he says: Before he gets up from his seat: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You, unless God forgives him for what he did in that seat of his.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, and this is his wording, and by Al-Nasa’i in Al-Yawm wa Al-Laylah from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak, and said its chain of transmission meets the conditions of Muslim, except that Al-Bukhari deemed it weak. I say: Imam Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Hatim, Abu Zur’ah, Al-Daraqutni and others deemed it weak, and they attributed the mistake in it to Ibn Jurayj. However, Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan from a chain of transmission other than Ibn Jurayj to Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Abu Dawud narrated it, and this is his wording, and Al-Nasa’i and Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak from Al-Hajjaj bin Dinar from Hashim, from Abu Al-Aliyah, from Abu Barzah Al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say at the end of his life, when he wanted to get up from a seat: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. You, I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.” A man said: O Messenger of God, you are saying something that you did not say before. He said: It is an expiation for what happens in the gathering. It has been narrated as a mursal on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, and God knows best. Thus, Al-Nasa’i and Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, from Abu Al-A’aliyah, from Rafi’ bin Khadij, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. It was also narrated as a mursal, and God knows best. Likewise, Abu Dawud narrated it from Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “There are words that no one utters in a gathering when he stands up three times, except that they will be an expiation for him, and no one says them in a gathering of good or a gathering of remembrance, except that he concludes his life with them as one concludes with a ring: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. There is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.” Al-Hakim included it from the hadith of the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, and he authenticated it, and from the narration of Jubayr bin Mut’im. Abu Bakr Al-Isma’ili narrated it from the Commander of the Believers, Umar bin Al-Khattab, all from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have devoted a separate section to that, mentioning its chains of transmission, wording, reasons, and what is related to it, and praise and thanks be to God. God the Almighty said: {And during part of the night, exalt Him} meaning, remember Him and worship Him by reciting and praying at night, as God the Almighty said: {And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.} God the Almighty said: {And at the setting of the stars}, as mentioned previously in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, that they are the two rak’ahs before the Fajr prayer, for they are prescribed when the stars set, that is, when they begin to disappear. Ibn Silan narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: {Do not abandon them, even if the horses chase you}, meaning the two rak’ahs of Fajr. Narrated by Abu Dawud. From this hadith, it was reported from some of the companions of Ahmad that they are obligatory, but it is weak due to the hadith: Five prayers during the day and night. He said: Do I have to do anything else? He said: No, unless you do it voluntarily. It was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was not more committed to any of the voluntary prayers than the two rak’ahs of Fajr. In a wording of Muslim: The two rak’ahs of Fajr are better than the world and everything in it. The last interpretation of Surat At-Tur, praise and thanks be to God.

Likewise, Abu Dawud narrated it from Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “There are words that no one utters in a gathering when he stands up three times, except that they will be an expiation for him, and no one says them in a gathering of good or a gathering of remembrance, except that he concludes his life with them as one concludes with a ring: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. There is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.” Al-Hakim included it from the hadith of the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, and he authenticated it, and from the narration of Jubayr bin Mut’im. Abu Bakr Al-Isma’ili narrated it from the Commander of the Believers, Umar bin Al-Khattab, all from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have devoted a separate section to that, mentioning its chains of transmission, wording, reasons, and what is related to it, and praise and thanks be to God. God the Almighty said: {And during part of the night, exalt Him} meaning, remember Him and worship Him by reciting and praying at night, as God the Almighty said: {And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.} God the Almighty said: {And at the setting of the stars}, as mentioned previously in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, that they are the two rak’ahs before the Fajr prayer, for they are prescribed when the stars set, that is, when they begin to disappear. Ibn Silan narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: {Do not abandon them, even if the horses chase you}, meaning the two rak’ahs of Fajr. Narrated by Abu Dawud. From this hadith, it was reported from some of the companions of Ahmad that they are obligatory, but it is weak due to the hadith: Five prayers during the day and night. He said: Do I have to do anything else? He said: No, unless you do it voluntarily. It was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was not more committed to any of the voluntary prayers than the two rak’ahs of Fajr. In a wording of Muslim: The two rak’ahs of Fajr are better than the world and everything in it. The last interpretation of Surat At-Tur, praise and thanks be to God.
